basis: Glycogen metabolism defect with polyglucosan accumulation and skeletal myopathy; cardiac involvement is not typical of this phenotype.
Inherited VWF coagulation defect; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish organ damage. Angiodysplasia is a separate vascular diagnosis.
Intracranial contents herniate into the nasal region, producing a congenital neural lesion and nasal airway mass; hydrocephalus occurs only in some cases.
Acid-base disorder; respiratory and renal causes vary across subtypes and do not establish shared organ damage.
Defective vitamin D activation causes mineral abnormalities and defining rickets; hepatic enzyme location does not imply liver damage.
Inherited mitochondrial metabolic defect presenting as skeletal myopathy; no evidence establishes additional commonly damaged organs.
Folate remethylation defect defined by central and peripheral neurologic disease; thrombosis and thromboembolic stroke occur in only 5-29%.
Omphalocele, laryngopharyngeal hypoplasia and scoliosis define the syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 80-99%. Facial and eyelid shape alone adds no axis.
UMP synthesis defect with anemia; developmental delay 80-99%, T-cell dysfunction 30-79%. Ureter, cardiac and hip abnormalities reported at 30-79% omitted by cap.
Bacterial infection directly ulcerates the esophageal mucosa.
Inhaled carbon and silica cause defining fibrosis of the lung parenchyma.
Hereditary predisposition to tumors of sympathetic neural lineage; metastatic sites and paraneoplastic complications are not established common involvement.
CMV infection directly causes pneumonia; underlying immunosuppression is a separate condition.
Inherited primary parathyroid hyperfunction; skeletal mineral loss affects roughly 30% or more. Renal stones are a separate complication.
Congenital ichthyosis limited to acral skin, with collodion membrane, hyperkeratosis and scaling.
Congenital finger flexion contractures define the umbrella; no supplied evidence establishes additional organ involvement across most subtypes.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma of lymphocytes; extranodal organ occupation is not established in most patients across this broad historical category.
Urothelial neoplasm arising in the urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Developmental brain, limb/joint and ear abnormalities characterize the syndrome; renal hypoplasia 6/6. Airway involvement lacks a reliable frequency and exceeds the cap.
Inherited congenital malformation of the external ear.
Central and peripheral neurodevelopmental degeneration defines the disorder; skeletal abnormalities occur in a small minority.
Pontocerebellar malformation and severe developmental impairment; strabismus 3/3 supports ocular dysfunction. Single-case hepatic and pleural findings lack reliable prevalence.
Testicular germ-cell tumor arises in reproductive tissue; no endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement is defined.
Meningeal tumor arising at the petroclival skull base; additional organ damage is not established as common.
Inherited metabolic bone disorder with excessive disorganized bone remodeling; renal and cardiovascular findings occur in only 5-29%.
